speaker: interviewer
text: Hey Marcus, thanks for jumping on. Is now still a good time?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yeah, I'm on my break, I've got a good half hour.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me a bit about your household and who does the food shopping.

speaker: interviewee
text: It's me, my partner Dana and her daughter, she's fifteen. I do the shopping mostly, I stop at the discount place on my way home from the warehouse. The only reason your app was even on my phone is the clutch went on the car and it sat in the garage for a week waiting on parts, and I wasn't carrying six bags home on the bus. Got the car back and that was that, discount place on the way home again.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. And how did you hear about Shmuber Eats?

speaker: interviewee
text: There was a flyer in the mailbox, I think. Or an ad on the bus. One of those.

speaker: interviewer
text: Got it. Walk me through your last order, from opening the app to putting things away.

speaker: interviewee
text: Okay so, I opened it, it asked for my address, I put in the basics. Chicken, rice, eggs, frozen veg, the yogurt Dana likes. Paid with my card. Then it showed me a picker name, and later a driver on the map. Bags came, I unpacked. Pretty normal.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Was anything confusing along the way?

speaker: interviewee
text: The first screen. It wanted me to pick a store before I could see anything, and I didn't know which store was which.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay, noted. And putting things away, anything there?

speaker: interviewee
text: One of the bags was the thin kind and it ripped on the stairs. The eggs survived though, so, a win.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. How often do you order groceries online?

speaker: interviewee
text: Hardly ever. I like to be in and out of the shop in fifteen minutes, I know where everything is.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Let's move on to the next one. Tell me about the last time an item in your order was substituted.

speaker: interviewee
text: They swapped the chicken thighs for drumsticks. That was a bit annoying because drumsticks are more bone, but it was the same price per pack, so whatever.

speaker: interviewer
text: And did you know about it before the bags came?

speaker: interviewee
text: There was a notification, I think, but I was at work. I don't look at my phone on the floor, you can't. So I found out at the door, basically.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. How do you keep track of what you need between orders?

speaker: interviewee
text: In my head. Dana sends me a text if she wants something specific. The kid just eats whatever's there.

speaker: interviewer
text: Would a shared list in the app be useful for you three?

speaker: interviewee
text: Maybe for Dana. I'd probably forget to look at it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. How did you pick the delivery window last time?

speaker: interviewee
text: I picked the latest one, eight to ten in the evening, so I'd be back from work. It came at like nine forty, which was fine.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. What would you think of a monthly delivery pass, and what would you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: Nah. I'm not paying monthly for something I use once in a blue moon. Maybe three, four a month, if it was like a streaming thing.

speaker: interviewer
text: What about 9.99 a month, with free delivery on every order?

speaker: interviewee
text: No way, not for me. That's a lot of chicken.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Fair enough. Great. On a scale of one to ten, how was the experience overall?

speaker: interviewee
text: Seven. It worked, nothing really went wrong. The app is a bit slow to open.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. Would you recommend it to a friend?

speaker: interviewee
text: Sure, if someone asked. I don't really go around recommending apps though.

speaker: interviewer
text: Totally. What would make you use it more?

speaker: interviewee
text: Honestly, if the evening slots went later. Eight to ten is the last one, and some weeks I'm on lates and I'm not home till eleven.

speaker: interviewer
text: Got it, later slots. Great. Did you use the app or the website?

speaker: interviewee
text: App. On my phone.

speaker: interviewer
text: And did the payment go through okay?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yeah, first time. Card was already saved from something else, I think.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Last question, is there anything about your orders I didn't ask about?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, I think that's it. Short and sweet.

speaker: interviewer
text: Perfect. Thanks so much Marcus, really appreciate it.

speaker: interviewee
text: No worries. Take care.
